workflow: Built-in ImageGen edits of actual orthographic model screenshots; no geometry deck panels.
ring_prompt: Create the ACTUAL REGISTERED TOP-VIEW UV PAINT MAP for the existing UFO ring. INPUT 1 is the orthographic screenshot/template of the real bare ring: this is the EDIT TARGET and its exact framing/geometry must govern the output. INPUT 2 shows the complete model only to locate the dome and six separate lamps; INPUT 3 is the approved painted UFO reference; INPUT 4 is the broader game's style guide. Do not create another generic material tile. Paint this exact annular model surface with hand-painted cobalt metal panels in the style of inputs 3 and 4. Keep the centre at exactly the image centre, outer vertex radius 49.02% of image width, inner hole radius 22.78%. Preserve the 48-sided outer/inner silhouette registration and the image crop. Artwork must align with this template. The first image's blue annulus becomes a convincing hand-painted UV surface: irregular staggered sheet-metal panel shapes, subtle overlapping RECTANGULAR/TRAPEZOID cover-plate shapes painted between the six lamp positions shown in input 2, broad cobalt/cerulean brush blocks, slate and blue-grey panels, some muted teal/violet undertones. Give each panel just a few confident broad dragged-bristle brush patches; avoid an all-over camouflage pattern. Panel joins are EXTREMELY THIN and intermittent darker blue paint marks, around 1-3 px at this size, not thick black outlines, not white borders, not a regular ring of pizza wedges, not uniform tiling. Add broken light blue-grey edge wear with a handful of short muted orange/ochre brush accents at selected plate corners, showing through blue overpainting, under 3% overall warm colour. The overall effect is stylized hand-painted alloy from the approved reference, not realistic grunge. The panel detail is painted into an albedo map, so no raised 3D extrusions, cast shadows or perspective. The lamps, dome and antenna are separate meshes: DO NOT paint any green lamps, circles for sockets, canopy, antenna, objects, labels, words or symbols into this map. Use image 2 only to leave sensible broad panel areas underneath those six mesh locations. Retain the neutral grey unused centre and background from image 1, but extend plain matching blue paint 12 pixels past both the inner and outer annulus edges as UV filtering bleed; don't place outlines along those boundaries. Square, fully opaque, exactly registered to input 1, no added margins or repositioning.
dome_prompt: Paint the FIRST input, the exact orthographic UV screenshot of the existing UFO's blue dome. The SECOND input is the approved UFO reference; THIRD is the game asset style guide. This must be an actual registered top-view UV paint map, not a generic swatch and not a new object render. Preserve the centred 20-sided disc silhouette exactly: centre image centre, outer vertex radius 49.02% of width. Paint INSIDE this dome footprint with the reference's faceted hand-painted blue canopy finish: deep cobalt, cerulean, slate/petrol blue and a little muted teal. LARGE deliberate painterly facet-shaped colour blocks, each with only a few broad dragged bristle strokes; avoid all-over checkerboard or camouflage. The canopy should be a little richer/darker than the ring, but still bright readable COBALT BLUE, never black or near-black plastic. A broad broken pale sky-blue brush reflection on the UPPER RIGHT, as in the reference, with a few smaller softer cool strokes elsewhere; painted reflections, not little circular white lamp glints or photoreal gloss. No tiny noise, black seams, grids, outlined facets, bolts, antenna, green lights, edge trim, symbols or text. No actual 3D dome shading, baked cast shadow, perspective or objects; all surface storytelling comes from painted colour blocks. Retain the neutral unused background outside the first screenshot's disc, with 12px of matching plain blue bleed beyond the disc for UV filtering. Square, fully opaque, exact screenshot registration. Treat the broad game style and actual original UFO reference as authoritative.
